Witchgrass is a warm-season fibrous-rooted ANNUAL, not a rhizomatous perennial. Published diffuse panicles ~13–50 cm, often breaking loose when ripe. Actual species panicle panel 3 and hairy-sheath panel 5 are useful, but neither proves a rooted annual or magnified tubercle-based hair origins. Never ID from a detached tumblehead alone.

Dallisgrass generally has conspicuous long silky hairs fringing its large spikelets; vaseygrass often has much more numerous finer racemes with smaller spikelets. Creeping wet-ground P. distichum typically has two terminal racemes and obvious stolons, while P. pubiflorum often has several racemes and larger spikelets. diagnostic_checks.compare: P. distichum has mostly two terminal near-digitate branches and more extensive runners; pubiflorum has fewer axillary heads reported.

diagnostic_checks.compare: P. pubiflorum normally 2.8–3.6 mm, P. floridanum is broader and up to ~4.1 mm; size ranges may approach one another.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA source checked; glandular hairs vary among varieties

diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect the tiny membrane and short rhizomatous crown

diagnostic_checks.compare: Urochloa signals have a much more obviously hairlike ciliate collar and DEVELOPED lower glume; species identity still requires spikelets.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA account; the nine named North American varieties prevent rigid hair/size rules

diagnostic_checks.look: Count exactly ONE MULTIFLORET spikelet at each true rachis node
diagnostic_checks.check: Cereal rye is an annual/biennial with a two-ranked laterally compressed flowering SPIKE: one spikelet per rachis node, carrying usually 2, sometimes 3 florets. This is fundamentally different from barley's three one-floret spikelets at one node.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Little barley has three separate spikelets at each node, normally with the central fertile and two lateral reduced; Elymus generally has two multi-floret spikelets per node.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA genus / accepted species treatment; complete attached spike node photo pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Secale genus

diagnostic_checks.look: Separate narrow awned GLUMES from long lemma AWNS
diagnostic_checks.check: The glumes are narrow, stiff, keeled and roughly 8–20 mm overall but their own terminal awns are usually only about 1–3 mm. Fertile lemmas about 14–18 mm taper to much longer straight/scabrous awns around 7–50 mm. Glumes and lemmas are different bracts.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Polypogon has conspicuous LONG glume awns; rye's longest visible awns generally arise from the fertile lemmas.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA Secale cereale, mature glume and lemma photograph at matched scale pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Secale cereale

diagnostic_checks.look: Find the short membranous ligule and wheat-like ears
diagnostic_checks.check: A cultivated/escaped cool-season annual or biennial with mostly fibrous roots, narrow clasping auricles (~0.5–1 mm), and a small usually truncate/lacerate MEMBRANOUS ligule. Cultivated spike may not shed its rachis easily, whereas wild forms can fragment.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Canada/Virginia Elymus are generally perennial and bear PAIRS of spikelets at nodes; the head silhouette may overlap rye when immature.
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA species and genus accounts; variety/site-specific grown rye images not independently certified
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Secale cereale

diagnostic_checks.look: Find the annual crown and heavy spike-like panicle
diagnostic_checks.check: Foxtail millet is an annual without persistent knotty rhizomes. FNA describes a stout, dense 8–30 cm panicle, sometimes lobed below, with mostly 1–3 bristles around each spikelet.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Setaria parviflora is perennial, rhizomatous and usually has 4–12 bristles under each spikelet
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA-backed; mature head and actual annual base photo pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Setaria italica

diagnostic_checks.look: Inspect the seed-bearing fertile lemma
diagnostic_checks.check: The mature upper lemma tends to be very finely transversely wrinkled to smooth/shiny and about 3 mm long; the upper floret may break away separately. The bristles remain sterile branchlets and are not 'awns'.
diagnostic_checks.compare: Marsh bristlegrass generally has a more conspicuously transversely wrinkled fertile lemma
diagnostic_checks.certainty: FNA-backed; domestication creates much variation; macro pending
diagnostic_checks.source: Flora of North America — Setaria italica
